content.comment_body: Been trying to capture data from one of my [product_name] devices for quite a while, but I’m not sure how to access the required data. Regarding the table you shared back in 2018—if I have data stored in AM3, can I read it directly from AM3 V1118.2 DB1,DBX1118.2, or do I need to log it to variable memory first? Are there any simple YouTube videos or guides that show step-by-step how to get this working? Thanks, [user_name]

Welcome to the forum. I need to apologize for an error in my previous PDF. The AM operand is actually a word operand (16 bits), not a bit operand. That means AM3 shouldn’t have the V1118.2 (DB1, DBX1118.2) address, but instead VW1122 (DB1, DBW1122). I’m attaching a corrected version of the [document].

Which platform are you using to read and write data? Are you working with Node-RED Modbus TCP, and if so, which nodes are you using? Different protocols such as S7 and the various Modbus variants require slightly different approaches. Sharing a screenshot or more details would help to better understand your setup.
I think there might be some misunderstanding regarding [user_name]'s issue.

Thanks for the quick replies—I'm still new to all this. I have three analog pt100 sensors and a switch connected; the goal is to capture temperature readings. I’ve successfully tested connectivity with Node-RED by switching Q4 from a Node-RED input and it works. Looking for advice on the best way to capture data from the [product_name] and get it into Node-RED. Cheers,
You mentioned an issue with AM3 in your first post. I’ve updated my PDF file. Could you clarify what specific problem you’re experiencing now?

I set up a connection and want to bring AM1-AM3 readings into Node-RED. I’ve also set up a connection with one AM1 variable, but I can’t seem to capture its value—think I’m doing something wrong. Regards,
I’ve got AM1 working in Node-RED using DB1,INT1118, based on a forum reference. But when I try mapping AM2 as DB1,INT1118.1, it still reads the AM1 input. Clearly I’m missing something. Thanks,
For help with Node-RED syntax, take a look at this web page: [url] node-red-contrib-s7. My PDF only shows the [company_name] S7 syntax.

As mentioned, I’m new to this. For reference, I’ve used: AM1 VW1118 DB1,DBW1118, AM2 VW1120 DB1,DBW1120, AM3 VW1122 DB1,DBW1122. I’ve set up these in Node-RED as: DW1,INT1118 - Reading 12, DW1,INT1119 - Reading 3072, DW1,INT1120 - Reading 11. The 12 and 11 respond to the temperature probes, but I can’t figure out INT1119. How do I relate your PDF info to what needs setting on the Node-RED node? I’m confused. Cheers,

Not sure what’s going wrong… For AM1 in the [product_name], it occupies VW1118 as an integer, made of two bytes: VB1118 and VB1119. VW1120 uses VB1120 and VB1121; VW1122 uses VB1122 and VB1123. Calling DB1,INT1119 in Node-RED mixes these bytes. Maybe posting your question in another conference related to IOT2000 might help—those experts know Node-RED better.

Don’t worry, I just had a similar moment—pulled all the wiring out of my [product_name]. I had activated four analogue inputs but didn’t read the bytes correctly. Checked all inputs individually, realized each is two bytes long, and had entered them sequentially. Sorry for the confusion.
No worries, mistakes are part of learning. Has your issue been resolved now?
[user_name] is correct about the 2-byte arrangement. For AM1 you should use DB1,INT1118 in Node-RED, for AM2 use DB1,INT1120—so each next AM input skips two bytes.
